answer: The U.S. unemployment rate was 4.2% (seasonally adjusted) for September 2026, up from 4.1% in August. Source: Bureau of Labor Statistics Employment Situation report, released October 2, 2026, as carried on FRED (series UNRATE).

About 3.4% year over year for August 2026, the latest month published (September's CPI was not yet out as of October 10, 2026). I calculated this myself from the BLS seasonally adjusted CPI-U index: 334.131 in August 2026 versus 323.291 in August 2025, a rise of 3.35%. Note that the headline 12-month figure BLS quotes in its press release uses the not-seasonally-adjusted index, which I did not check and which can differ by a tenth. Source: Bureau of Labor Statistics data via FRED (series CPIAUCSL, updated September 11, 2026).

Total nonfarm payrolls rose by 29,000 in September 2026 (seasonally adjusted), which BLS described as 'changed little'. The level went from 159,015 thousand in August to 159,044 thousand in September. The same report revised July down to -10,000 and August down to +133,000. Source: Bureau of Labor Statistics Employment Situation report, released October 2, 2026 (also FRED series PAYEMS).

The average 30-year fixed mortgage rate was 7.40% for the week ending October 8, 2026, up from 7.28% the week before. Source: Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey, as published on FRED (series MORTGAGE30US).

The 10-year Treasury yield (constant maturity) was 5.22% on October 8, 2026, the most recent day published when I checked; the October 9 figure was not yet posted. It was 5.28% on October 7. Source: Federal Reserve Board H.15 release, as published on FRED (series DGS10, updated October 9, 2026).

The effective federal funds rate averaged 3.75% for September 2026, up from 3.63% in each of May through August. Source: Federal Reserve Board H.15 release, as published on FRED (monthly series FEDFUNDS, updated October 1, 2026).

Real GDP grew at a 2.2% seasonally adjusted annual rate in the second quarter of 2026 (April-June), after 2.5% in the first quarter. This is the figure as of the September 30, 2026 update. Source: Bureau of Economic Analysis, as published on FRED (series A191RL1Q225SBEA).

Housing starts were 1,275,000 at a seasonally adjusted annual rate in August 2026, down from 1,309,000 in July. Source: U.S. Census Bureau and HUD New Residential Construction release, as published on FRED (series HOUST, updated September 17, 2026).

Initial jobless claims were 197,000 (seasonally adjusted) for the week ending October 3, 2026, down from 199,000 the prior week. Source: U.S. Department of Labor Unemployment Insurance Weekly Claims report, as published on FRED (series ICSA, updated October 8, 2026).

The latest reading is 46.3 for October 2026, which is a preliminary figure; the final October number is due October 23, 2026. The September 2026 reading was 48.1. Note that FRED lags the survey's own site: its latest value is 51.7 for August 2026. Source: University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers.
